```{r blind-switch}
UNBLIND <- as.logical(Sys.getenv("UNBLIND_STUDY2", "FALSE"))
# The blind switch, as in Study2_01_Quant.Rmd. While UNBLIND is FALSE this
# file reads the blind long data file, shuffles its source labels again and
# shuffles the ratings right after the ratings are built (section 2.1), and
# writes every output to a blind_run/ subfolder of the folder its real
# counterpart goes to. A value that is neither TRUE nor FALSE stops the run.
if (is.na(UNBLIND)) stop("UNBLIND_STUDY2 must be TRUE or FALSE.")

# A blind report belongs in blind_run/, and an unblinded report beside this
# file. The knit: line in the header reads the same environment variable and
# sends the report to the right folder when the file is knitted with
# RStudio's Knit button. A call to rmarkdown::render() must pass
# output_dir = "blind_run" in a blind run and leave it out in an unblinded
# run. A run whose report would land in the wrong folder stops here, before
# anything is written. The folder is read from the settings render() is
# running with; a knit that does not go through render() is not checked.
render_output_dir <- function() {
  frame <- Find(function(e) exists("output_dir", envir = e, inherits = FALSE) &&
                  exists("knit_input", envir = e, inherits = FALSE),
                sys.frames())
  if (is.null(frame)) return(NULL)
  d <- get("output_dir", envir = frame)
  normalizePath(if (is.null(d)) "." else d, mustWork = FALSE)
}
report_dir <- render_output_dir()
if (!UNBLIND && !is.null(report_dir) && basename(report_dir) != "blind_run") {
  stop("A blind report must be written to blind_run/. Knit with the Knit ",
       "button, or run rmarkdown::render(\"Study2_03_Integration.Rmd\", ",
       "output_dir = \"blind_run\").")
}
if (UNBLIND && !is.null(report_dir) && basename(report_dir) == "blind_run") {
  stop("An unblinded report must not be written to blind_run/. Set the ",
       "environment variable UNBLIND_STUDY2 to TRUE before knitting, or run ",
       "rmarkdown::render(\"Study2_03_Integration.Rmd\") without output_dir.")
}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(echo = TRUE, message = FALSE, warning = TRUE,
                      fig.align = "center")
```

```{r banner, echo=FALSE, results='asis'}
if (!UNBLIND) {
  cat("**Blind run. The source labels are shuffled across participants and",
      "the ratings across the responses to each question, so nothing in this",
      "report is a result.**\n")
} else {
  cat("**Unblinded run on the real source labels and ratings.**\n")
}
```

# 0. What this file does

`Study2_02_Text.ipynb` measured the 20,659 justifications without seeing the
condition or the rating. This file joins those two back onto the measures and
runs what registration question 8
(`Docs/Preregistration/AsPredicted/Study2_AsPredicted.md`) names for the
text.

Two checks, fixed for every study in the Study 1 registration, are registered
for the creativity justifications (section 3):

1. how well the words alone predict the rating and the source condition in
   participants left out of fitting, by ridge regression;
2. whether AI-condition participants reuse their own words across their
   creativity justifications more than Human-condition participants,
   relative to others writing about the same second work.

A response is about one second work, a source image at one modification
level, so the second work is the stimulus of both checks.

Everything else is exploratory description with no verdict (section 4): the
same two checks on the transformativeness and essence justifications, tone and
concreteness from published word ratings, topics found by a model given no
labels, and the words the first check leans on most when it predicts the
rating and the source condition.

Every justification was written after its rating, so none is read as the
rating's cause. What follows describes what people wrote once their number
was chosen.

# 1. Setup

## 1.1 Packages

```{r packages}
# dplyr, tidyr, tibble and readr build and write the tables. lme4 and
# lmerTest fit the mixed models of section 4. glmnet fits the penalised
# regressions, and Matrix stores the word counts. The two registered checks
# come from the shared helper text_checks.R.
suppressPackageStartupMessages({
  library(dplyr)
  library(tidyr)
  library(tibble)
  library(readr)
  library(lme4)
  library(lmerTest)
  library(Matrix)
  library(glmnet)
})
```

## 1.2 Paths

```{r paths}
# Every path is found from this file's own folder, which is the working
# directory when the file is knitted. STUDY2_DIR names the Study 2 folder
# instead, and STUDY_SHARED_R the folder of the shared R helpers. Printed
# paths are relative to the Study 2 folder.
STUDY_DIR <- normalizePath(Sys.getenv("STUDY2_DIR", getwd()), mustWork = TRUE)
SHARED_R  <- Sys.getenv("STUDY_SHARED_R",
                        file.path(STUDY_DIR, "..", "shared", "R"))
source(file.path(SHARED_R, "fit_status.R"))
source(file.path(SHARED_R, "text_checks.R"))

mode_dir <- function(dir) if (UNBLIND) dir else file.path(dir, "blind_run")
OUT_STUDY  <- mode_dir(STUDY_DIR)
OUT_TABLES <- mode_dir(file.path(STUDY_DIR, "tables"))
dir.create(OUT_TABLES, recursive = TRUE, showWarnings = FALSE)

NLP_DIR     <- file.path(STUDY_DIR, "nlp")
TEXT_TABLES <- file.path(STUDY_DIR, "tables")
INPUTS <- c(
  long_data   = file.path(OUT_STUDY, "study2_long_with_text.csv"),
  measures    = file.path(NLP_DIR, "study2_text_measures.csv"),
  wordcounts  = file.path(NLP_DIR, "study2_text_wordcounts.csv"),
  vocabulary  = file.path(NLP_DIR, "study2_text_vocabulary.csv"),
  tokens      = file.path(NLP_DIR, "study2_text_tokens.csv"),
  affect      = file.path(NLP_DIR, "study2_text_affect.csv"),
  topics      = file.path(NLP_DIR, "study2_text_topics.csv"),
  topic_words = file.path(TEXT_TABLES, "study2_text_topics_top_words.csv")
)
QUANT_MANIFEST <- file.path(OUT_TABLES, "study2_quant_run_manifest.csv")
TEXT_MANIFEST  <- file.path(TEXT_TABLES, "study2_text_run_manifest.csv")
missing_inputs <- names(INPUTS)[!file.exists(INPUTS)]
if (length(missing_inputs) > 0) {
  stop("Missing input(s): ", paste(missing_inputs, collapse = ", "),
       ". Knit Study2_01_Quant.Rmd in the same mode and run ",
       "Study2_02_Text.ipynb first.")
}
for (p in names(INPUTS)) cat(sprintf("%-12s %s\n", p, relative_path(INPUTS[[p]], STUDY_DIR)))
cat("Tables to:  ", relative_path(OUT_TABLES, STUDY_DIR), "\n")

SEED           <- 20260421L
MEASURES       <- c("transformativeness", "essence_change", "creativity")
REGISTERED_DIM <- "creativity"
OTHER_DIMS     <- c("transformativeness", "essence_change")
SOURCE_LEVELS  <- c("Human", "AI")
KEY            <- c("id", "stimulus_id", "dimension")
N_RESPONSES    <- 20659L
N_PARTICIPANTS <- 235L
```

## 1.3 Run record

```{r run-record}
# The run record stores the SHA-256 checksum of every input (a 64-character
# fingerprint of the file's exact bytes), deletes the previous run's manifest
# now and each output's previous copy before the chunk that writes it, and
# writes the manifest last.
run <- start_run_record(INPUTS,
                        file.path(OUT_TABLES, "study2_integration_run_manifest.csv"),
                        STUDY_DIR)
write_run_inputs(run, file.path(OUT_TABLES, "study2_integration_run_inputs.csv"))
cat("Run identifier:", run$run_id, "\n")

# Each input must be the file its producing run recorded. The long data file
# is checked against the manifest of Study2_01_Quant.Rmd in the same mode,
# and the text tables against the notebook's manifest. A manifest on disk
# means its run reached the end.
if (!file.exists(QUANT_MANIFEST) || !file.exists(TEXT_MANIFEST)) {
  stop("A run manifest is missing. Knit Study2_01_Quant.Rmd in the same mode ",
       "and run Study2_02_Text.ipynb to the end first.")
}
quant_manifest <- read_csv(QUANT_MANIFEST, show_col_types = FALSE)
text_manifest  <- read_csv(TEXT_MANIFEST, show_col_types = FALSE)
recorded <- bind_rows(
  select(quant_manifest, file, sha256),
  select(text_manifest, file, sha256))
input_check <- tibble(input = names(INPUTS),
                      file  = relative_path(INPUTS, STUDY_DIR),
                      sha256 = run$inputs$sha256) %>%
  left_join(rename(recorded, recorded_sha256 = sha256), by = "file") %>%
  mutate(matches_its_manifest = sha256 == recorded_sha256)
print(as.data.frame(select(input_check, input, file, matches_its_manifest)))
if (!all(input_check$matches_its_manifest %in% TRUE)) {
  stop("Some input is not the file its producing run recorded.")
}
cat("The notebook measured", unique(text_manifest$input_file), "\n")
```

# 2. The ratings and the text tables

## 2.1 The ratings, and the blind shuffle

```{r ratings}
# One row per response: the participant, the second work, the question, the
# rating and the source condition. The second work, work_id in the long
# data, names the source image and the modification level shown, and it is
# the stimulus of every check below.
long <- read_csv(INPUTS[["long_data"]], show_col_types = FALSE,
                 col_types = cols(.default = col_character(),
                                  rating = col_integer(),
                                  k_points = col_integer()),
                 na = "")
expected_mode <- if (UNBLIND) "real" else "shuffled"
if (!all(long$label_mode == expected_mode)) {
  stop("The long data says label_mode ", paste(unique(long$label_mode), collapse = ", "),
       ", and this run needs ", expected_mode, ". Knit Study2_01_Quant.Rmd in the ",
       "same mode first.")
}
ratings <- long %>%
  transmute(id, stimulus_id = work_id, dimension, rating, source)
stopifnot(nrow(ratings) == N_RESPONSES, n_distinct(ratings$id) == N_PARTICIPANTS,
          !anyDuplicated(ratings[, KEY]), all(ratings$source %in% SOURCE_LEVELS),
          !anyNA(ratings$rating), all(long$k_points == 5))

# In a blind run the source labels are shuffled here, after the ratings are
# built and before any summary or model, with the method and seed of
# Study2_01_Quant.Rmd. The blind long data file already carries shuffled
# labels; shuffling them again keeps this file blind whichever long data file
# it is given.
#
# The rating carries no label to shuffle, so in a blind run it is shuffled
# itself. Within each question, the ratings are dealt again among the
# responses. Each question keeps its ratings and their spread, and every link
# between a rating and its participant, second work, justification and
# source is cut. Without this step the parts of this file that relate the
# words to the rating alone, such as the rating-from-words check of section
# 3.1 and the lasso of section 4.4, would be real results. Responses are
# taken in byte order of their identifiers, and the random-number state is
# put back afterwards.
shuffle_rating_within_dimension <- function(df, seed) {
  ord <- order(df$dimension, df$id, df$stimulus_id, method = "radix")
  had_seed <- exists(".Random.seed", envir = globalenv(), inherits = FALSE)
  if (had_seed) old_seed <- get(".Random.seed", envir = globalenv())
  on.exit({
    if (had_seed) assign(".Random.seed", old_seed, envir = globalenv())
    else if (exists(".Random.seed", envir = globalenv(), inherits = FALSE)) {
      rm(".Random.seed", envir = globalenv())
    }
  }, add = TRUE)
  set.seed(seed)
  out <- df
  for (dim in sort(unique(df$dimension), method = "radix")) {
    rows <- ord[df$dimension[ord] == dim & !is.na(df$rating[ord])]
    out$rating[rows] <- df$rating[rows][sample.int(length(rows))]
  }
  out
}

if (!UNBLIND) {
  ratings_before <- ratings
  ratings <- blind_shuffle(ratings, "id", "source", seed = SEED)
  ratings <- shuffle_rating_within_dimension(ratings, seed = SEED)
  stopifnot(identical(sort(table(distinct(ratings, id, source)$source)),
                      sort(table(distinct(ratings_before, id, source)$source))))
  for (dim in MEASURES) {
    stopifnot(identical(sort(ratings$rating[ratings$dimension == dim]),
                        sort(ratings_before$rating[ratings_before$dimension == dim])))
  }
  rm(ratings_before)
  cat("Blind run: source labels shuffled across participants and ratings",
      "within each question, seed", SEED, "\n")
}
ratings <- ratings %>% mutate(source = factor(source, levels = SOURCE_LEVELS))
cat("Responses:", nrow(ratings), "| participants:", n_distinct(ratings$id),
    "| second works:", n_distinct(ratings$stimulus_id), "\n")
```

## 2.2 The text tables and their contract

```{r text-tables}
# Every text table must carry its agreed columns and none of the forbidden
# ones (the condition, the labels the models use, the rating, the text). The
# readers in text_checks.R stop if one does.
FORBIDDEN <- c(TEXT_FORBIDDEN_COLS, "source", "modification", "image_kind")
measure_cols <- c("id", "stimulus_id", "stimulus_image", "stimulus_type",
                  "stimulus_modification", "dimension", "n_words",
                  "says_detail", "says_time", "says_skill", "says_concept",
                  "says_prompt", "says_machine_made", "machine_made_reading",
                  "prior_exposure", "anchor_echo",
                  "detail_polarity", "time_polarity", "skill_polarity",
                  "concept_polarity")
measures <- read_csv(INPUTS[["measures"]], show_col_types = FALSE,
                     col_types = cols(.default = col_character(),
                                      n_words = col_integer()),
                     na = character())
check_text_table(measures, measure_cols, "The measures file", forbidden = FORBIDDEN)

wordcounts <- read_text_wordcounts(INPUTS[["wordcounts"]])
vocabulary <- read_text_vocabulary(INPUTS[["vocabulary"]])
tokens     <- read_text_tokens(INPUTS[["tokens"]])

affect <- read_csv(INPUTS[["affect"]], show_col_types = FALSE,
                   col_types = cols(id = col_character(), stimulus_id = col_character(),
                                    dimension = col_character(),
                                    n_content_words = col_integer(),
                                    n_vad_matched = col_integer(), valence = col_double(),
                                    arousal = col_double(), dominance = col_double(),
                                    n_conc_matched = col_integer(),
                                    concreteness = col_double()))
check_text_table(affect, c(KEY, "n_content_words", "n_vad_matched", "valence",
                           "arousal", "dominance", "n_conc_matched",
                           "concreteness"), "The affect file", forbidden = FORBIDDEN)
topics <- read_csv(INPUTS[["topics"]], show_col_types = FALSE,
                   col_types = cols(id = col_character(), stimulus_id = col_character(),
                                    dimension = col_character(), topic = col_integer(),
                                    weight = col_double()))
check_text_table(topics, c(KEY, "topic", "weight"), "The topic file", forbidden = FORBIDDEN)
topic_words <- read_csv(INPUTS[["topic_words"]], show_col_types = FALSE,
                        col_types = cols(dimension = col_character(),
                                         topic = col_integer(), rank = col_integer(),
                                         word = col_character(), weight = col_double()))
check_text_table(topic_words, c("dimension", "topic", "rank", "word", "weight"),
                 "The topic word list", forbidden = FORBIDDEN)

# Every table keyed by response names exactly the responses of the ratings.
response_keys <- function(df) sort(unique(paste(df$id, df$stimulus_id, df$dimension)))
rating_keys <- response_keys(ratings)
for (nm in c("measures", "tokens", "affect", "topics")) {
  stopifnot(identical(response_keys(get(nm)), rating_keys))
}
cat("Every table keyed by response names the same", length(rating_keys),
    "responses as the ratings.\n")
```

## 2.3 Joining the measures to the ratings and the condition

```{r join}
# The measures were computed without the condition or the rating. They are
# joined back here on the participant, the second work and the question, one
# row to one row.
run_clear_outputs(run, file.path(OUT_TABLES, "study2_text_join_check.csv"))
joined <- measures %>%
  inner_join(ratings, by = KEY, relationship = "one-to-one")
join_check <- tibble(
  rows_in_measures = nrow(measures),
  rows_in_ratings  = nrow(ratings),
  rows_joined      = nrow(joined),
  only_in_measures = nrow(anti_join(measures, ratings, by = KEY)),
  only_in_ratings  = nrow(anti_join(ratings, measures, by = KEY)))
print(as.data.frame(join_check))
stopifnot(join_check$rows_joined == N_RESPONSES, join_check$only_in_measures == 0,
          join_check$only_in_ratings == 0)
write_csv(join_check, file.path(OUT_TABLES, "study2_text_join_check.csv"))
```

# 3. The two registered checks, on creativity

## 3.1 How closely the words track the rating and the condition

```{r recoverability}
# The first check asks how well the words alone predict the rating, and how
# well they predict the source condition, in participants left out of
# fitting. The model is ridge regression (a regression that shrinks each
# word's weight toward zero), scored on ten folds grouped by participant, so
# no participant is on both the fitting and the scoring side. For the rating
# the score is the Pearson correlation between predicted and observed
# ratings. For the condition it is the AUC, the probability that a randomly
# chosen AI response gets a higher predicted probability of the AI condition
# than a randomly chosen Human response; one half is chance. Each score has a
# 95 percent interval from resampling participants and a permutation null,
# the same pipeline rerun on shuffled outcomes 200 times. Every setting is
# Study 1's, set as the defaults of text_recoverability(), and the reading
# rule is recoverability_readings(). The check is descriptive and enters no
# correction family.
run_clear_outputs(run,
                  file.path(OUT_TABLES, "study2_text_wordcount_check.csv"),
                  file.path(OUT_TABLES, "study2_text_recoverability.csv"))

wordcount_check <- check_text_wordcounts(ratings, wordcounts, vocabulary,
                                         stim_cols = "stimulus_id", arm_col = "source",
                                         arm_levels = SOURCE_LEVELS)
print(as.data.frame(wordcount_check))
write_csv(wordcount_check, file.path(OUT_TABLES, "study2_text_wordcount_check.csv"))

with_readings <- function(tab) {
  tab %>% left_join(recoverability_readings(tab) %>%
                      select(dimension, target, predictors, reading),
                    by = c("dimension", "target", "predictors"))
}
recover <- text_recoverability(ratings, wordcounts, dims = REGISTERED_DIM,
                               stim_cols = "stimulus_id", arm_col = "source",
                               arm_levels = SOURCE_LEVELS) %>%
  with_readings() %>%
  mutate(role = "registered", .after = dimension)
stopifnot(nrow(recover) == 5)
write_csv(recover, file.path(OUT_TABLES, "study2_text_recoverability.csv"))
print(as.data.frame(select(recover, dimension, target, predictors, estimate,
                           ci_low, ci_high, null_95th, status, reading)), digits = 3)
```

## 3.2 Within-person word overlap by condition

```{r self-overlap}
# The second check predicts that AI-condition participants reuse their own
# words across their creativity justifications more than Human-condition
# participants, relative to others writing about the same second work. For
# each participant, the own-word overlap is the mean Jaccard overlap (the
# words two texts share divided by the words either uses) across that
# participant's creativity justifications, and the stranger baseline is the
# overlap of each justification with other participants' justifications of
# the same second work. Their difference is regressed on the condition with
# the mean number of words as a covariate. The interval and p-value come from
# 2,000 resamples of participants within each condition, with the stranger
# baseline rebuilt in each. One measure is registered, so the Holm
# correction is over one test. The reading is supported, opposite direction
# or inconclusive.
run_clear_outputs(run,
                  file.path(OUT_TABLES, "study2_text_selfsimilarity_by_arm.csv"),
                  file.path(OUT_TABLES, "study2_text_selfsimilarity_per_person.csv"))
overlap <- text_self_overlap(ratings, tokens, dims = REGISTERED_DIM,
                             stim_cols = "stimulus_id", arm_col = "source",
                             arm_levels = SOURCE_LEVELS)
overlap$by_arm <- overlap$by_arm %>% mutate(registered = TRUE, .after = role)
stopifnot(sum(overlap$by_arm$role == "registered comparison") == 1,
          nrow(overlap$per_person) == N_PARTICIPANTS)
write_csv(overlap$by_arm,
          file.path(OUT_TABLES, "study2_text_selfsimilarity_by_arm.csv"))
write_csv(overlap$per_person,
          file.path(OUT_TABLES, "study2_text_selfsimilarity_per_person.csv"))
print(as.data.frame(overlap$by_arm %>%
                      filter(role == "registered comparison") %>%
                      select(dimension, quantity, estimate, ci_lo, ci_hi,
                             p_raw, p_holm, reading, status)), digits = 3)
```

# 4. Exploratory description

Everything in this section is exploratory. It describes what participants
wrote after choosing their rating, and none of it tests a prediction.

## 4.1 The two checks on the other two measures

```{r other-measures}
# The same two checks, with the same settings, on the transformativeness and
# essence justifications. Each measure is run on its own, so each overlap
# p-value is corrected over one test, and none of these rows carries a
# registered verdict.
run_clear_outputs(run,
                  file.path(OUT_TABLES, "study2_text_recoverability_other_measures.csv"),
                  file.path(OUT_TABLES, "study2_text_selfsimilarity_other_measures.csv"))
recover_other <- text_recoverability(ratings, wordcounts, dims = OTHER_DIMS,
                                     stim_cols = "stimulus_id", arm_col = "source",
                                     arm_levels = SOURCE_LEVELS) %>%
  with_readings() %>%
  mutate(role = "exploratory", .after = dimension)
overlap_other <- bind_rows(lapply(OTHER_DIMS, function(dim) {
  text_self_overlap(ratings, tokens, dims = dim, stim_cols = "stimulus_id",
                    arm_col = "source", arm_levels = SOURCE_LEVELS)$by_arm
})) %>%
  mutate(role = if_else(role == "registered comparison", "exploratory comparison", role),
         p_holm = NA_real_, reading = NA_character_) %>%
  mutate(registered = FALSE, .after = role)
stopifnot(nrow(recover_other) == 10,
          sum(overlap_other$role == "exploratory comparison") == 2)
write_csv(recover_other,
          file.path(OUT_TABLES, "study2_text_recoverability_other_measures.csv"))
write_csv(overlap_other,
          file.path(OUT_TABLES, "study2_text_selfsimilarity_other_measures.csv"))
print(as.data.frame(select(recover_other, dimension, target, predictors, estimate,
                           ci_low, ci_high, null_95th, status, reading)), digits = 3)
print(as.data.frame(overlap_other %>%
                      filter(role == "exploratory comparison") %>%
                      select(dimension, quantity, estimate, ci_lo, ci_hi,
                             p_raw, status)), digits = 3)
```

## 4.2 Tone and concreteness

```{r affect}
# Each justification's mean valence (how pleasant its words are, 1 to 9),
# arousal (how excited they make a reader feel, 1 to 9), dominance (how much
# in control they make a reader feel, 1 to 9) and concreteness (how much they
# refer to things that can be seen or touched, 1 to 5), from Warriner,
# Kuperman and Brysbaert (2013) and Brysbaert, Warriner and Kuperman (2014),
# as the notebook scored them. A response with no matched word has no score
# and drops out of that model. The model is Study 1's, per question and
# measure:
#
#   score ~ source x rating_c + (1 | participant) + (1 | second work)
#
# where rating_c is the rating minus that question's mean rating, so the
# source coefficient (AI minus Human, the Human condition as the reference)
# is the difference at the average rating. The 24 p-values of the two
# coefficients are corrected by Benjamini-Hochberg, which holds the expected
# share of false positives among the rows called positive. The correction
# makes a long table easier to read; it does not make it confirmatory.
run_clear_outputs(run, file.path(OUT_TABLES, "study2_text_affect_by_arm.csv"))

CONTROL <- lmerControl(optimizer = "bobyqa")
rating_centres <- ratings %>% group_by(dimension) %>%
  summarise(rating_centre = mean(rating), .groups = "drop")
scored <- ratings %>%
  left_join(rating_centres, by = "dimension") %>%
  mutate(rating_c = rating - rating_centre)

AFFECT_MEASURES <- c("valence", "arousal", "dominance", "concreteness")
AFFECT_TERMS <- c(
  "sourceAI"          = "source difference (AI minus Human) at the average rating",
  "sourceAI:rating_c" = "source by rating interaction (AI minus Human, per rating point)")

fit_log <- list()
tidy_terms <- function(res, terms) {
  if (res$status$fit_error) {
    return(tibble(term = terms, estimate = NA_real_, std_error = NA_real_,
                  df = NA_real_, t = NA_real_, p_raw = NA_real_))
  }
  co <- summary(res$fit)$coefficients
  tibble(term = terms, estimate = co[terms, "Estimate"],
         std_error = co[terms, "Std. Error"], df = co[terms, "df"],
         t = co[terms, "t value"],
         p_raw = na_unless_usable(co[terms, "Pr(>|t|)"], res$status))
}

affect_rows <- list()
for (dim in MEASURES) {
  for (m in AFFECT_MEASURES) {
    d <- affect %>% filter(dimension == dim, !is.na(.data[[m]])) %>%
      inner_join(scored, by = KEY, relationship = "one-to-one") %>%
      mutate(score = .data[[m]])
    res <- fit_with_status(lmerTest::lmer(
      score ~ source * rating_c + (1 | id) + (1 | stimulus_id), data = d,
      REML = TRUE, control = CONTROL))
    step <- paste0("4.2 ", m, " ~ source x rating, ", dim)
    fit_log[[step]] <- res$status %>% mutate(step = step, dimension = dim,
                                             n_obs = nrow(d), .before = 1)
    affect_rows[[step]] <- tidy_terms(res, names(AFFECT_TERMS)) %>%
      mutate(dimension = dim, measure = m, .before = 1) %>%
      mutate(quantity = unname(AFFECT_TERMS[term]),
             ci_lo = na_unless_usable(estimate - qt(0.975, df) * std_error, res$status),
             ci_hi = na_unless_usable(estimate + qt(0.975, df) * std_error, res$status),
             mean_Human = mean(d$score[d$source == "Human"]),
             mean_AI    = mean(d$score[d$source == "AI"]),
             n_scored   = nrow(d),
             n_participants = n_distinct(d$id),
             converged = res$status$converged, singular = res$status$singular,
             note = fit_note(res$status),
             model = paste0(m, " ~ source * rating_c + (1 | id) + (1 | stimulus_id), REML, bobyqa"))
  }
}
affect_by_arm <- bind_rows(affect_rows)
affect_by_arm <- affect_by_arm %>%
  mutate(p_bh = p.adjust(p_raw, method = "BH", n = nrow(affect_by_arm)),
         .after = p_raw)
stopifnot(nrow(affect_by_arm) == 24)
write_csv(affect_by_arm, file.path(OUT_TABLES, "study2_text_affect_by_arm.csv"))
print(as.data.frame(select(affect_by_arm, dimension, measure, term, estimate,
                           ci_lo, ci_hi, p_bh, converged, singular)), digits = 3)
```

## 4.3 Topics found by a model given no labels

```{r topics}
# The notebook fitted a topic model to each question without the condition
# or the rating, and gave each justification a weight on each topic, the
# weights summing to one. The model is Study 1's, per question and topic:
#
#   weight ~ source + rating_c + (1 | participant) + (1 | second work)
#
# Topic weights are bounded and pile up at zero, so the source term is
# tested against a permutation null: the source labels are dealt again among
# the participants, each keeping one label, the model is refitted and the
# source term's t value is recorded, 200 times. The p-value is the share of
# shuffles, counting the observed data as one, whose t value is at least as
# far from zero as the observed one. The same 200 shuffles serve every topic
# of a question, they are drawn from the seed before the parallel section
# starts, and the p-values are corrected by Benjamini-Hochberg within each
# question. Each topic is labelled by its five heaviest words.
run_clear_outputs(run, file.path(OUT_TABLES, "study2_text_topics_by_arm.csv"))

N_TOPIC_PERM <- 200L
topic_labels <- topic_words %>% filter(rank <= 5) %>% arrange(dimension, topic, rank) %>%
  group_by(dimension, topic) %>%
  summarise(topic_label = paste(word, collapse = ", "), .groups = "drop")
topics_joined <- topics %>% filter(!is.na(weight)) %>%
  inner_join(scored, by = KEY)

# The source term's t value from one refit; a refit that fails gives NA and
# is counted.
topic_t <- function(d) {
  fit <- tryCatch(suppressWarnings(suppressMessages(
    lme4::lmer(weight ~ source + rating_c + (1 | id) + (1 | stimulus_id), data = d,
               REML = TRUE, control = CONTROL))),
    error = function(e) NULL)
  if (is.null(fit)) return(NA_real_)
  co <- summary(fit)$coefficients
  if (!"sourceAI" %in% rownames(co)) NA_real_ else unname(co["sourceAI", "t value"])
}

topic_rows <- list()
for (dim in MEASURES) {
  d_dim  <- topics_joined %>% filter(dimension == dim)
  id_arm <- distinct(d_dim, id, source)
  id_arm <- id_arm[order(id_arm$id, method = "radix"), ]
  set.seed(SEED)
  shuffles <- replicate(N_TOPIC_PERM,
                        setNames(sample(as.character(id_arm$source)), id_arm$id),
                        simplify = FALSE)
  for (k in sort(unique(d_dim$topic))) {
    d <- d_dim %>% filter(topic == k)
    res <- fit_with_status(lmerTest::lmer(
      weight ~ source + rating_c + (1 | id) + (1 | stimulus_id), data = d,
      REML = TRUE, control = CONTROL))
    step <- paste0("4.3 topic ", k, " weight ~ source + rating, ", dim)
    fit_log[[step]] <- res$status %>% mutate(step = step, dimension = dim,
                                             n_obs = nrow(d), .before = 1)
    usable <- fit_usable(res$status)
    co <- if (res$status$fit_error) NULL else summary(res$fit)$coefficients
    t_obs <- if (is.null(co)) NA_real_ else unname(co["sourceAI", "t value"])
    t_null <- text_run_permutations(shuffles, function(lab) {
      dd <- d
      dd$source <- factor(lab[dd$id], levels = SOURCE_LEVELS)
      topic_t(dd)
    }, text_default_workers())
    n_valid <- sum(!is.na(t_null))
    topic_rows[[step]] <- tibble(
      dimension = dim, topic = k,
      quantity  = "source difference in topic weight (AI minus Human) at the same rating",
      estimate  = if (is.null(co)) NA_real_ else unname(co["sourceAI", "Estimate"]),
      std_error = if (usable) unname(co["sourceAI", "Std. Error"]) else NA_real_,
      t         = if (usable) t_obs else NA_real_,
      p_perm    = if (!usable || is.na(t_obs) || n_valid == 0) NA_real_ else
        (1 + sum(abs(t_null) >= abs(t_obs), na.rm = TRUE)) / (1 + n_valid),
      n_perm = N_TOPIC_PERM, n_perm_valid = n_valid, perm_seed = SEED,
      rating_estimate = if (is.null(co)) NA_real_ else unname(co["rating_c", "Estimate"]),
      mean_weight_Human = mean(d$weight[d$source == "Human"]),
      mean_weight_AI    = mean(d$weight[d$source == "AI"]),
      n_responses = nrow(d), n_participants = n_distinct(d$id),
      converged = res$status$converged, singular = res$status$singular,
      note = fit_note(res$status),
      model = "weight ~ source + rating_c + (1 | id) + (1 | stimulus_id), REML, bobyqa; source term tested against source labels shuffled across participants")
  }
}
topics_by_arm <- bind_rows(topic_rows) %>%
  group_by(dimension) %>%
  mutate(p_bh = p.adjust(p_perm, method = "BH", n = n()), .after = p_perm) %>%
  ungroup() %>%
  left_join(topic_labels, by = c("dimension", "topic")) %>%
  relocate(topic_label, .after = topic)
stopifnot(nrow(topics_by_arm) == nrow(distinct(topics, dimension, topic)))
write_csv(topics_by_arm, file.path(OUT_TABLES, "study2_text_topics_by_arm.csv"))
print(as.data.frame(select(topics_by_arm, dimension, topic, topic_label, estimate,
                           p_perm, p_bh, n_perm_valid, converged, singular)),
      digits = 3)
```

## 4.4 The words the first check leans on most

```{r prediction-weights}
# The first check (section 3.1) asks how well the words predict the rating
# and the source condition, with ridge models that spread small weights over
# every word. This asks which words do the predicting, with the lasso, a
# penalised regression whose penalty sets most word weights to exactly zero,
# so only the words a prediction cannot do without keep one. As in Study 1,
# there are two models per measure:
#
#   rating  a lasso linear regression of the rating on the word counts;
#   arm     a lasso logistic regression of the source condition (AI against
#           Human) on the word counts, with the rating in the model and left
#           unpenalised (penalty factor 0), so a word keeps a weight only if
#           it tells the conditions apart beyond what the rating does.
#
# The penalty is chosen by ten-fold cross-validation grouped by participant,
# with the vocabulary rebuilt inside each training fold by the five-response
# floor. The held-out loss is the squared error for the rating and the
# binomial deviance (minus twice the log-likelihood of the held-out
# conditions) for the source. The chosen penalty is lambda.1se, the strongest
# penalty whose cross-validated loss is within one standard error of the
# best. The model is then refitted on every response at that penalty, and
# the words with a nonzero weight are reported with their signs. A weight is
# the change in the rating, or in the log-odds of the AI condition, for one
# more use of the word, after the shrinkage. Among words that move together
# the lasso tends to keep one, so a word missing from the list may still go
# with the outcome. None of this tests a word.
run_clear_outputs(run, file.path(OUT_TABLES, "study2_text_prediction_weights.csv"))

prepared <- prepare_text_ratings(ratings, "stimulus_id", "source", SOURCE_LEVELS)
wc_keyed <- wordcounts %>% mutate(.stim = stimulus_key(wordcounts, "stimulus_id"))

# The held-out loss of a matrix of predictions, one column per penalty, on
# the response scale. Probabilities are kept a little away from zero and
# one, as glmnet does.
heldout_loss <- function(pred, y, family) {
  if (family == "binomial") {
    p <- pmin(pmax(pred, 1e-5), 1 - 1e-5)
    -2 * (y * log(p) + (1 - y) * log(1 - p))
  } else {
    (y - pred)^2
  }
}

lasso_weights <- function(dim, target) {
  fr     <- text_dimension_frame(prepared, wc_keyed, dim)
  resp   <- fr$resp
  counts <- fr$counts
  is_arm <- target == "arm"
  family <- if (is_arm) "binomial" else "gaussian"
  y      <- if (is_arm) as.integer(resp$arm == SOURCE_LEVELS[2]) else resp$rating

  set.seed(TEXT_SEED)
  outer_by_id <- text_participant_folds(fr$id_arm, TEXT_N_OUTER_FOLDS, SOURCE_LEVELS)
  outer_fold  <- unname(outer_by_id[resp$id])

  # The source model carries the rating as its first column, unpenalised.
  build_x <- function(words) {
    X <- text_response_word_matrix(resp, counts, words)
    if (is_arm) {
      X <- cbind(Matrix::Matrix(resp$rating, ncol = 1, sparse = TRUE,
                                dimnames = list(NULL, "rating")), X)
    }
    X
  }
  penalty <- function(X) if (is_arm) c(0, rep(1, ncol(X) - 1)) else rep(1, ncol(X))

  vocab_all <- text_floor_vocabulary(resp, counts, rep(TRUE, nrow(resp)),
                                     TEXT_WORD_MIN_RESPONSES)
  X_all  <- build_x(vocab_all$word)
  fitted <- text_with_warnings(glmnet::glmnet(X_all, y, family = family, alpha = 1,
                                              penalty.factor = penalty(X_all)))
  full_fit <- fitted$value
  lam      <- full_fit$lambda
  warns    <- fitted$warnings

  fold_loss <- matrix(NA_real_, TEXT_N_OUTER_FOLDS, length(lam))
  fold_n    <- integer(TEXT_N_OUTER_FOLDS)
  for (k in seq_len(TEXT_N_OUTER_FOLDS)) {
    tr <- outer_fold != k
    Xk <- build_x(text_floor_vocabulary(resp, counts, tr, TEXT_WORD_MIN_RESPONSES)$word)
    fk <- text_with_warnings(glmnet::glmnet(Xk[tr, , drop = FALSE], y[tr],
                                            family = family, alpha = 1,
                                            lambda = lam,
                                            penalty.factor = penalty(Xk)))
    warns <- c(warns, fk$warnings)
    pk <- predict(fk$value, Xk[!tr, , drop = FALSE], s = lam, type = "response")
    fold_loss[k, ] <- colMeans(heldout_loss(as.matrix(pk), y[!tr], family))
    fold_n[k]      <- sum(!tr)
  }
  cvm  <- apply(fold_loss, 2, weighted.mean, w = fold_n)
  cvsd <- sqrt(apply(sweep(fold_loss, 2, cvm)^2, 2, weighted.mean, w = fold_n) /
                 (TEXT_N_OUTER_FOLDS - 1))
  i_min      <- which.min(cvm)
  lambda_1se <- max(lam[cvm <= cvm[i_min] + cvsd[i_min]])

  warns  <- unique(warns)
  status <- if (length(warns) == 0) "ok" else "nonconvergence"
  b <- as.matrix(coef(full_fit, s = lambda_1se))[, 1]
  rating_coef <- if (is_arm) unname(b["rating"]) else NA_real_
  b <- b[setdiff(names(b), c("(Intercept)", "rating"))]
  b <- b[b != 0]
  words_tbl <- if (length(b) == 0) {
    tibble(word = NA_character_, coefficient = NA_real_, sign = NA_character_,
           rank = NA_integer_, n_responses_word = NA_integer_)
  } else {
    tibble(word = names(b), coefficient = unname(b)) %>%
      mutate(sign = ifelse(coefficient > 0, "positive", "negative"),
             rank = as.integer(rank(-abs(coefficient), ties.method = "first"))) %>%
      left_join(rename(vocab_all, n_responses_word = n_responses), by = "word") %>%
      arrange(rank)
  }
  model_text <- if (is_arm) {
    paste0("lasso logistic regression (glmnet, alpha = 1), source condition ",
           "(AI against Human) on the rating (penalty factor 0) and the word ",
           "counts; penalty at lambda.1se from ten-fold cross-validation ",
           "grouped by participant with the vocabulary rebuilt in each ",
           "training fold; refitted on all responses")
  } else {
    paste0("lasso linear regression (glmnet, alpha = 1), rating on the word ",
           "counts; penalty at lambda.1se from ten-fold cross-validation ",
           "grouped by participant with the vocabulary rebuilt in each ",
           "training fold; refitted on all responses")
  }
  words_tbl %>%
    mutate(dimension = dim, target = target,
           predictors = if (is_arm) "words, with the rating unpenalised" else "words",
           .before = 1) %>%
    mutate(rating_coefficient = rating_coef,
           lambda_1se = lambda_1se, lambda_min = lam[i_min],
           n_words_in_model = nrow(vocab_all), n_nonzero = length(b),
           cv_loss = if (is_arm) "binomial deviance" else "squared error",
           n_folds = TEXT_N_OUTER_FOLDS,
           seed = TEXT_SEED, n_responses = nrow(resp), status = status,
           note = if (length(warns) == 0) "status ok; no warning from any fit" else
             paste0("status nonconvergence; ", paste(warns, collapse = "; ")),
           model = model_text)
}

LASSO_TARGETS <- c("rating", "arm")
prediction_weights <- bind_rows(lapply(MEASURES, function(dim) {
  bind_rows(lapply(LASSO_TARGETS, function(tg) lasso_weights(dim, tg)))
}))
stopifnot(nrow(distinct(prediction_weights, dimension, target)) ==
            length(MEASURES) * length(LASSO_TARGETS))
write_csv(prediction_weights, file.path(OUT_TABLES, "study2_text_prediction_weights.csv"))
for (dim in MEASURES) {
  for (tg in LASSO_TARGETS) {
    pw <- filter(prediction_weights, dimension == dim, target == tg)
    cat(dim, tg, "model (", pw$status[1], "):", pw$n_nonzero[1], "of",
        pw$n_words_in_model[1], "words keep a weight at lambda.1se\n")
  }
}
```

# 5. Fit status

```{r fit-log}
# One row per step that fits a model: the mixed models of sections 4.2 and
# 4.3, and the two checks of sections 3 and 4.1, which report their own
# status (ok, nonconvergence or error) from the warnings their fits raised.
run_clear_outputs(run, file.path(OUT_TABLES, "study2_text_fit_log.csv"))
check_status <- function(tab, step, kind) {
  tab %>% distinct(dimension, status, note) %>%
    transmute(step = step, dimension, kind = kind,
              fit_error = status == "error", converged = status == "ok",
              singular = NA, lme4_messages = note, usable = status == "ok")
}
fit_log_tbl <- bind_rows(
  bind_rows(fit_log) %>% mutate(kind = "linear mixed model",
                                usable = !fit_error & converged),
  check_status(recover, "3.1 recoverability, registered", "ridge regressions"),
  check_status(overlap$by_arm %>% filter(role == "registered comparison"),
               "3.2 within-person overlap, registered", "ordinary least squares"),
  check_status(recover_other, "4.1 recoverability, exploratory", "ridge regressions"),
  check_status(overlap_other %>% filter(role == "registered comparison"),
               "4.1 within-person overlap, exploratory", "ordinary least squares"),
  prediction_weights %>% distinct(dimension, target, status, note) %>%
    transmute(step = paste0("4.4 lasso word weights, ", target, " model"), dimension,
              kind = "lasso regression",
              fit_error = status == "error", converged = status == "ok",
              singular = NA, lme4_messages = note, usable = status == "ok")
) %>% relocate(step, dimension, kind, usable)
print(as.data.frame(select(fit_log_tbl, step, dimension, usable, fit_error,
                           converged, singular)))
write_csv(fit_log_tbl, file.path(OUT_TABLES, "study2_text_fit_log.csv"))
lmm_log <- filter(fit_log_tbl, kind == "linear mixed model")
cat("Mixed models in section 4:", nrow(lmm_log), "| converged:", sum(lmm_log$converged),
    "| singular:", sum(lmm_log$singular %in% TRUE), "| errored:",
    sum(lmm_log$fit_error), "\n")
cat("Registered checks, status: recoverability", unique(recover$status),
    "| overlap", unique(overlap$by_arm$status), "\n")
```
